chunks: And from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ‘Ajlān, who said:

Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him) stood by the grave of a man and said: O Allāh! Connect with him in his loneliness; keep him company in his desolation; and descend Your Mercy on him in a way that he will not need the mercy of others.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited for the deceased at the grave according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Bāqir (peace be upon him) recited this supplication at the grave of a believer, invoking divine comfort to alleviate the soul's desolation in the grave (Barzakh). The prayer emphasizes self-sufficiency through God's mercy, ensuring the deceased remains independent of the mercy of other creatures, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatological traditions regarding the intermediate state.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 14. My father narrated to me from Ḥusain ibn Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from Ibn ‘Ajlān, who said:

Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) stood next to the grave of a man and said: O Allāh! Connect with him in his loneliness; keep him company in his desolation; and descend Your Mercy on him in a way that he will not need the mercy of others.
